Catalogued (§40), report row (TODO on the branch), registry §40 (fixed_in undef, checker format-body-lexed-as-code now names §40).  NOT FIXED: the brief put the format token LAST and the batch checkpointed before it; Pl::Parser::_strip_format_blocks stays.

=== s527g ===
NOT FIXED (checkpoint, budget).  Design measured: PPI has no format support at all.  Token half (mine): a new token class for the picture text (sibling of HereDoc), started when `format [NAME] =` ends a line at a statement start, consuming the lines up to and including the lone `.` line -- source-contiguous, so round-trip is trivial; inert for PCL (Pl::Parser::_strip_format_blocks blanks the lines before PPI sees them, and PCL already keeps the statements after the `.` -- probed: perl and PCL both print `after` / `end` for two formats).  Lexer half (s527f's): end the format statement at the body token (today it runs on into `write;`).  Only with both can _strip_format_blocks go.
subject: PPI: a FORMAT body (`format NAME =` ... `.`) is tokenized as CODE -- perl reads it as picture text (scan_formline); PPI's statement then swallows what follows the `.` (t/op/gv.t, t/op/rt119311.t, t/comp/parser.t cascades)
